goal: Put a mesh on screen, before or after the scene is running
without: Without a material, addToScene and registerScene succeed and the mesh is in scene.meshes, but nothing is built or drawn for it; the shape factories (createBox, createSphere, createGround, ...) assign none, while createLines and the other line factories assign a line material themselves.
Assigning the material later, even after registerScene, builds the mesh on the following frames; no second registerScene is needed.

goal: Make a box cast a shadow from a directional light onto the ground
without: Without sun.shadowGenerator = sg (creating it does not link it; addToScene(scene, sg) neither links nor lists it), no map is drawn or sampled.
Without setShadowTaskCasterMeshes no map is drawn.
With registerScene instead there is no shadow task: no map, ever.
Without receiveShadows = true before registering (setting it later is not picked up), the ground does not sample the map.

goal: Hide a mesh for a while and show it again
steps:
setMeshVisible(crate, false); // also hides everything in crate.children
setMeshVisible(crate, true);
without: With removeFromScene instead, the mesh is retired: its children are removed with it, and after the next frame addToScene(scene, crate) throws "cannot be added" (unless another scene still holds the mesh).
A hidden mesh is left out of createDefaultCamera's framing.

goal: Attach a mesh to a parent so it moves, hides and is removed with it
without: With only wheel.parent = pivot, the world matrix follows pivot but pivot.children stays empty: addToScene(scene, pivot) does not add wheel, setMeshVisible(pivot, false) does not hide it, and removeFromScene(scene, pivot) leaves it in the scene.
After children.push alone, wheel.parent is null until addToScene sets it.

goal: Change a light's brightness or color while the scene runs
without: A plain write (sun.intensity = 2, sun.diffuse = [...], sun.diffuse[0] = 1, spot.range = 10) is not uploaded: the shaders keep the old value until a tracked change uploads the lights again.
Without _bumpLightVersion after writing a hemispheric light's colors, they are not uploaded (setLightDiffuseColor does not fit it: it has diffuseColor, not diffuse).

goal: Keep a directional light's shadow map covering all casters, thin instances included
without: The PCF and ESM maps start 1 unit in front of the light's position ((0, 0, 0) unless placed), so a caster behind it, or under 1 unit in front, gets light-space depth below 0 and is left out of the map; place the light past the farthest caster.
The map is fitted to each caster's boundMin/boundMax through its world matrix only, so thin instances outside those bounds land outside the map; enableThinInstanceWorldBounds does not change that.

goal: Draw many copies of a mesh and move, add or remove them
steps:
const mats = new Float32Array(16 * n); // column-major, xyz at [12..14]
setThinInstances(tree, mats, n); // keeps a reference to mats
mats[16 * i + 12] = 5; flushThinInstances(tree); // after edits
setThinInstanceMatrix(tree, i, m); // no flush needed
removeThinInstance(tree, i); // the LAST instance moves into slot i
const j = addThinInstance(tree, m); // may replace tree.thinInstances.matrices
without: Without flushThinInstances, in-place edits are not uploaded.
After removeThinInstance(i), the former last instance is index i; an index kept for it is stale.
Once addThinInstance outgrows the pool it copies to a new array; edits to your old array are then not seen, so write to tree.thinInstances.matrices.
addThinInstance on a mesh without instances starts a pool of 16.

goal: Give a mesh that is already drawing thin instances or per-instance colors
steps:
setThinInstances(rock, mats, n); // rock was built by registerScene
setThinInstanceColors(rock, colors); // RGBA: 4 floats per instance
markMeshRenderableDirty(rock); // or: await rebuildSceneRenderables(scene)
without: Without markMeshRenderableDirty (or rebuildSceneRenderables), a mesh built without instances never gets an instance buffer, and instance colors first set after the build are never uploaded; no error.
Set before registerScene, or on a new mesh before it is added to a running scene, they need no extra call.

goal: Add fog to the scene and change it later
steps:
setFog(scene, { mode: 3, density: 0, start: 10, end: 60, color: [0.5, 0.6, 0.7] }); // 1 exp, 2 exp2, 3 linear
await registerScene(scene); // fog is compiled into the shaders here
setFog(scene, { ...scene.fog!, end: 30 }); // later change: a NEW object
without: With setFog only after registerScene, no shader has fog until await rebuildSceneRenderables(scene).
With scene.fog = {...} instead of setFog, fog is compiled in but its uniforms are never written; mode stays 0, which the shader treats as no fog.
Editing the fog object in place (scene.fog.end = 30) is not uploaded.

goal: Let a light reach some meshes and not others
without: A change to these sets after the scene is built has no effect on a mesh until its world matrix changes or a light is added to or removed from the scene.
mesh.id is unset by default, so includedOnlyMeshIds holding mesh names leaves those meshes unlit by that light.

goal: Switch a light's shadows off and on at runtime
without: With removeFromScene(scene, sun) instead, the generator is unlinked: sun.shadowGenerator is undefined, and adding the light back does not restore it.

With nothing changed the map is not redrawn; a caster's world-matrix or thin-instance change, a light position/direction .set(), setLightIntensity or setLightDiffuseColor redraws it, a plain sun.intensity write does not.

steps:
setMaxLights(32);
await registerScene(scene); // call setMaxLights before this
without: Without setMaxLights, lights past the 16th stay in scene.lights but are not uploaded, with no error; the cap counts the whole scene, not one material.

goal: Run per-frame logic in a set order
without: Registered as separate callbacks, they run in reverse: the one registered last runs first.
With fixedDeltaMs at 0 (the default), ms is the frame's delta in milliseconds.

goal: Point a default camera at a thin-instanced field
without: Without enableThinInstanceWorldBounds, the camera frames only the prototype's own bounds at the mesh's position.
It frames what is in scene.meshes at the call, skipping hidden meshes; meshes added later do not reframe it.

goal: Make copies of a mesh that can be added and removed on their own
without: Cloning after the original was removed from its last scene (and a frame passed) throws "cannot be cloned"; clone first.
Removing the original retires only it; the clone keeps the shared buffers until it too leaves its last scene.
